items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I did some things with him on Capitol

ctx.x: But I was glad to -- it gave me a chance to really display some versatility, you know, because I could perform as a single artist or with -- when I say single I mean with rhythm and piano, and/or with a big orchestra. That was -- but the arrangements were built around me and for me, and I give -- really, I give both of these men credit. Harold Mooney on

Capitol.

Also, Billy May didn't do a bad job. I did some things with him on Capitol, although this is sort of coming to me in the --Billy May was also a very wonderful man, very wonderful. I did some things with him too, but the things with Harold Mooney were a little different, because that was my time to experiment with strings, you know, which sort of gave a little -- a little something extra, you know, to what I'd done, and I'm very proud of that.

The thing that I regret today is the fact that none of the record companies, they're not releasing any of my material, any of these things that I did, and it hurts a little bit because this is one of the ways that you make money in the business, you know. You're not just in it for your health or because you like to do it. I enjoy it. I love what I do.
